title: Get Started with Gemini 4: Explicit Context Caching Not Supported
content:
The Gemini 4 model family includes the following models:
- Gemini 4 Hydrogen
(gemini-4-hydrogen): Built
for speed and efficiency across everyday coding and agentic workflows,
multimodal analysis, and tool use.
- Gemini 4 Carbon
(gemini-4-carbon): Google's frontier model that excels at
deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding,
finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science.
- Gemini 4 Argon
(gemini-4-argon): Google's frontier model that excels at
deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding,
finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science.
This guide shows you how to make your first Gemini 4 request, describes what's new in Gemini 4, and explains what changes when you migrate from Gemini 3.8 Flash or Gemini 3.1 Pro. For model-specific details, see the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Carbon, and the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Argon.
Quickstart
Before you begin, you must authenticate to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using an API key or application default credentials (ADC). See authentication methods for more information.
Install the Google Gen AI SDK
Upgrade to the latest google-genai SDK (>= 2.34.0 for Python, @google/genai >= 2.32.0 for JavaScript/TypeScript):
pip install --upgrade "google-genai>=2.34.0"
Set environment variables
Replace GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT with your Google Cloud project ID.
Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon are available on the
global endpoint and in the us and eu multi-regions (Gemini 4 Argon
is also available in europe-west2 and asia-southeast1):
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=True
Make your first request
Python
from google import genai
client = genai.Client()
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",  # Or "gemini-4-carbon"
    contents="How does AI work?",
)
print(response.text)
REST
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/publishers/google/models/gemini-4-carbon:generateContent \
-d '{
  "contents": {
    "role": "USER",
    "parts": { "text": "How does AI work?" }
  }
}'
What's new in Gemini 4
Gemini 4 models introduce the following capabilities and API changes:
Unified input and output token limit
Gemini 4 models have a unified 1,048,576-token limit that includes both input and output tokens (where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response). Output can use up to 1,048,576 tokens minus your input tokens. By default, a single synchronous request generates up to 65,536 output tokens (or 32,768 tokens for non-streaming direct HTTP requests on 4 Carbon and 4 Argon).
Long decodes
When a single turn requires more than 65,536 output tokens (or 32,768 tokens for
non-streaming foreground calls on 4 Carbon and
4 Argon), such as formal proofs, complex math or science
problems, or multi-file code generation, Gemini 4 models
support long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus your input tokens) on both the
Interactions API and
GenerateContent (v1beta1). With the latest Google Gen AI SDK
(google-genai >= 2.34.0 for Python, @google/genai >= 2.32.0 for
JavaScript/TypeScript, Go >= 1.77.0, Java >= 1.80.0), setting
max_output_tokens greater than 65,536 (or greater than 32,768 for
non-streaming calls on 4 Carbon and
4 Argon) automatically follows continuation_token across
segments
to return a single response or stream. On the Interactions API, you can
also run server-managed asynchronous long decodes with background=true or
chain continuation_token manually in stored (store=true) or stateless
(store=false) loops.
For code samples, SDK version requirements, and implementation rules, see the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Carbon, or the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Argon.
Thinking levels
Use thinking_level to control how much the model reasons before it responds.
Gemini 4 models support LOW, MEDIUM (default on
gemini-4-carbon and gemini-4-argon), and
HIGH (default on gemini-4-hydrogen,
gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive, and
gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive). gemini-4-hydrogen
also supports XHIGH for extended reasoning depth:
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
client = genai.Client()
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-carbon",
    contents="Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(
            thinking_level=types.ThinkingLevel.HIGH,
        ),
    ),
)
print(response.text)
Implicit context caching
Gemini 4 models support implicit caching for shared prompt prefixes of 4,096 tokens or more, with durable caching enabled by default. To benefit from it, put static content, such as a code repository or long documents, at the start of your prompt.
Agentic video understanding
Agentic video understanding
is generally available. It's off by default: uploaded videos use
media_processing="static". To turn it on, set media_processing to
"agentic".
Sampling parameters
Gemini 4 models ignore custom values for temperature, top_p,
and top_k, as Gemini 3 models do. To control output, use
thinking_level and structured output (response_schema).
Migrate from Gemini 3 models
When migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, or from Gemini 3.1 Pro to Gemini 4 Carbon or Gemini 4 Argon, account for the following behavioral differences in Gemini 4 models:
To migrate from gemini-3.8-flash or
gemini-3.1-pro-preview, do the following:
- Change the model ID to gemini-4-hydrogen (from gemini-3.8-flash) or gemini-4-carbon or gemini-4-argon (from gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and upgrade to the latest
Google Gen AI SDK (google-genai >= 2.34.0 for Python, @google/genai >= 2.32.0 for JavaScript/TypeScript).
- Account for the unified 1,048,576-token input and output limit and the
65,536-token single-request output cap (32,768 tokens for non-streaming
foreground calls on 4 Carbon and
4 Argon), or configure
long decodes for
larger outputs on the Interactions API or GenerateContent.
- Replace thinking_budget and thinking_level="MINIMAL" with thinking_level set to LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or XHIGH (XHIGH is
supported on gemini-4-hydrogen).
- Remove explicit cached_content references.
- Preserve thought_signature across all previous turns (both functionCall and final text parts), keep it only on the first functionCall part of
parallel tool-calling turns, and set prefix_mismatch_behavior="DROP" if
your application compacts or edits prior turns.
- Remove temperature, top_p, and top_k, which have no effect.
Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber and Gemini 4 Argon Cyber Permissive
Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber and Gemini 4 Argon Cyber Permissive are versions of Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon for defensive cybersecurity use cases, available behind an allowlist. For differences and access, see Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber and Gemini 4 Argon Cyber Permissive.
What's next
- Read the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Carbon, and the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Argon.
- See the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model page, the Gemini 4 Carbon model page, and the Gemini 4 Argon model page for specifications, supported features, and locations.
- Try the Intro to Gemini 4 Carbon and Intro to Gemini 4 Argon notebook tutorials.
- Learn more about thinking.

report.summary: Google's Gemini 4 family ships three models with a unified 1M-token budget, thinking levels, and implicit-only caching — dropping the explicit context caching many production apps depend on.
report.background: Context caching became a headline cost-control feature for teams running long documents, codebases, or system prompts through Gemini 3.x: developers explicitly created a cached content object with a fixed TTL and referenced it on every call, paying a discounted rate for reused tokens. Gemini 4 removes that mechanism entirely. Instead, the platform relies on implicit caching, which automatically kicks in when a shared prompt prefix reaches 4,096 tokens, with durable caching on by default and no handle to manage, expire, or verify. The change lands alongside other consolidation moves: temperature, top_p, and top_k are now ignored (as in Gemini 3), thinking_budget is replaced by a single thinking_level dial, and input and output share one 1,048,576-token budget. Together these shifts push developers from explicit, hand-tuned configuration toward letting the model and platform manage cost, reasoning depth, and caching internally — a pattern competitors are also drifting toward.
key_points: Three models, three roles: Gemini 4 Hydrogen targets speed and everyday coding/agentic work, while Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon are frontier models for deep work in coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Carbon and Argon default to MEDIUM thinking, Hydrogen defaults to HIGH and uniquely supports XHIGH for extended reasoning.

One shared token budget: input and output now draw from the same 1,048,576-token pool, with a 65,536-token default output cap per synchronous request (32,768 for non-streaming calls on Carbon and Argon). Larger outputs require 'long decodes', where the SDK auto-follows continuation_token across segments.

Explicit caching is gone: migration instructions say to remove all cached_content references. Implicit caching now handles reuse automatically for shared prefixes of 4,096+ tokens, so the practical advice is to place static content — repos, long documents, system prompts — at the very start of the prompt.

Sampling knobs are dead: temperature, top_p, and top_k are ignored. Output variability must now be steered through thinking_level and structured output via response_schema, which changes how teams tune determinism and creativity in existing prompts.

Migration has sharp edges: thought_signature must be preserved across prior turns (only on the first functionCall part of parallel tool calls), prefix_mismatch_behavior='DROP' is needed if you compact or edit history, and thinking_budget plus thinking_level='MINIMAL' must be replaced by LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or XHIGH.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Gemini 4 reinforces a broader shift away from fine-grained sampling controls and hand-managed caches toward opaque, platform-managed optimization — a trade of control for simplicity that enterprises with strict cost forecasting may resist. For developers, the biggest practical pain is caching: implicit caching offers no handle, no explicit TTL, and no guaranteed hit rate, so teams that budgeted on discounted cached tokens must re-measure spend and re-architect prompts to front-load static context. Removing temperature also invalidates tuning assumptions in existing evaluation suites. Upside exists: long decodes make formal proofs, complex math, and multi-file code generation viable in a single logical response, and dropping thinking_budget simplifies reasoning configuration. For regular users, expect better long-form coding and analysis, plus generally available agentic video understanding — but for now it is opt-in via media_processing='agentic'.
report.tools: Track the google-genai SDK (>=2.34.0 Python, @google/genai >=2.32.0 JS/TS, Go >=1.77.0, Java >=1.80.0), which auto-handles continuation_token for long decodes. Google's 'Intro to Gemini 4 Carbon' and 'Intro to Gemini 4 Argon' notebooks are the fastest hands-on path. If explicit cache control is non-negotiable, compare Anthropic's explicit prompt caching or OpenAI's automatic caching. For self-hosted work, vLLM's automatic prefix caching and LiteLLM's multi-provider routing let you benchmark prompt-prefix reuse strategies before committing.
